summary: Tubuai Airport (TUB/NTAT) is a medium-sized regional airport serving Tubuai, the main island of the Austral Islands archipelago, the southernmost island group in French Polynesia. Located on a flat coastal plain near Mataura, the airport provides the primary air link between Tubuai and Tahiti (Papeete), roughly 640 km to the northwest. The region is historically significant as one of the earliest Polynesian-influenced islands explored by Europeans and was among the first places the HMS Bounty mutineers settled after leaving Tahiti in 1789.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Tubuai Airport?
A: Air Tahiti is the primary carrier serving Tubuai Airport, offering scheduled flights to and from Papeete (PPT) on Tahiti. Flights are limited, typically operating a few times per week.

Q: How long is the flight from Tubuai to Papeete?
A: The flight to Papeete takes approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes, covering around 640 km of Pacific Ocean.

Q: When is the best time to visit Tubuai?
A: The dry season from June to September offers the most pleasant weather, with cooler temperatures and less rainfall. Peak travel months align with these drier conditions.

Q: Are there any international flights into Tubuai?
A: No, Tubuai Airport handles only domestic flights within French Polynesia. International travelers typically arrive first at Fa'a'ā International Airport in Papeete before connecting onward.
transport_tips: Tubuai is a small island, so the airport is only a short drive from the main settlement of Mataura. Car rentals and shuttle services are available but limited, so arranging transport in advance is strongly recommended. Taxis may not always be waiting upon arrival, so booking accommodation transfers ahead of time is the most reliable option. There is no public bus service between the airport and surrounding villages.
local_tip: Arriving passengers should bring cash in CFP francs (XPF), as most local shops, restaurants, and rental agencies on Tubuai do not accept credit cards. ATMs are limited and sometimes out of service on outer islands.
